newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB buys shares in Polish bank.
newsitem.headline: AIB buys shares in Polish bank.

text.p: The investment arm of Allied Irish Banks said on Thursday it had acquired 6.5 million shares of Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy S.A. (WBK) from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

AIB European Investments Limited said the shares represent 9.4 percent of the issued share capital of WBK and were bought for a consideration of 90.7 million zloty or 18.9 million Irish pounds at 13.95 zloty a share.
AIB entered into an option agreement with the EBRD in early 1995 giving the Irish bank the right to purchase EBRD's 23.9 percent holding in WBK. It acquired 16.3 percent of shares in February 1995.
To complete the deal under Polish stock exchange regulations the transaction is being carried out in two stages.
These are the purchase of 6.5 million shares followed by a bid for all other shares of WBK at the same price, the bank said.
When both stages of the transaction are carried out, AIB's total shareholding in WBK should increase to 60.2 percent at a total cost of about 96.2 million Irish pounds, it said.

It said a bid for all the other shares would be made in due course. The price, while higher than one mentioned in recent AIB statements, represents a substantial discount from the current market price of 21 zloty per WBK share, it said.
AIB Group Chief Executive Tom Mulcahy said the decision "is evidence of our satisfaction with the progress of WBK since we made our original investment in early 1995."
WBK is a regional commercial bank with headquarters in Poznan and is one of the top 10 Polish banks. It declared pretax profits last year of 220.7 million zloty.
